text: SEBI Report: 93% of individual F&O traders lost money with an average loss of ₹2 Lakhs. Overtrading was the primary contributor.
source: SEBI Study on Retail F&O Traders, 2023

text: Revenge trading turns a ₹2,000 loss into a ₹50,000 catastrophe. The market doesn't care about your ego.
The market will be here tomorrow. Your capital might not be if you trade right now.
Between 10:30 AM and 1:15 PM, option premiums bleed due to theta decay and low volume. This is where retail traders donate money to institutions.
Professional traders wait for setups. Amateur traders chase every candle. The edge is in patience, not in screen time.
source: Mark Douglas — Trading in the Zone

text: The best trade you'll ever make is the one you didn't take. Discipline is the compound interest of trading.
90% of your profits will come from 10% of your trades. The other 90% of trades are just noise that erodes your capital.
A trader who takes 15 trades a day isn't trading — they're gambling with extra steps. Max 2–3 high-conviction setups per day.
Your stop loss is your friend. Your overtrading habit is your enemy. One protects capital, the other destroys it.
The urge to trade right now is your cortisol talking, not your strategy. Step away. Drink water. Go for a walk.
Every professional trader has a rule: when in doubt, stay out. The opportunity cost of a bad trade is far greater than missing a move.
You don't need to trade every day. You need to be solvent every day. Capital preservation is the only edge that never expires.
The sideways chop between 10:30 AM and 1:15 PM creates false breakouts that trap retail traders. Institutions use this range to accumulate.
If your P&L is red and your finger is hovering over 'Buy' — that's revenge trading. Close the app. The loss is already taken.
Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most. You want a trade now. You want a funded account forever.
